issue.title: just check can fail after every selected test passes when the pytest-current tmpdir symlink disappears during xdist cleanup
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-na.1--1 (epic sase-na, plan 202608/word_completion_ranking.md) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP, and carried forward here by sase-na.land because it is unrelated to that epic's word-ranking work.

Reported symptom: 'just check' can exit non-zero after its scoped pytest lane has already reported that every selected test passed. The reporter attributed this to a race in pytest's tmpdir cleanup that runs after xdist workers finish, where the 'pytest-current' symlink under the base temp directory is removed by one process while another is still resolving it, so the run fails during teardown rather than on any test assertion.

Honest state of the evidence: the original note is the only observation. sase-na.land did not reproduce it while landing the epic on master eba0eab73 in workspace sase_12 -- 'just test-scoped' passed 1493 tests cleanly, and several targeted pytest runs over tests/history, tests/ace/tui/widgets, and tests/ace/tui completed without a teardown failure. So this is an intermittent race whose trigger conditions are not yet characterized, not a deterministic defect. The sizing reflects that: the root cause is genuinely unknown and the first real work is reproducing it under load.

Impact if real: a spurious red on the mandatory pre-reply gate is expensive, because the failure appears after a fully green test report and gives an agent no failing node to act on, so the natural response is to rerun the whole gate.

Scope: reproduce the teardown failure (most likely under repeated parallel 'just check' / 'just test-scoped' runs, possibly with concurrent runs from sibling workspaces sharing a base temp directory), capture the actual traceback and exit path, then make the cleanup tolerate a concurrently removed 'pytest-current' link rather than failing the run. If it cannot be reproduced after a bounded effort, close with that finding recorded -- do not paper over it by suppressing teardown errors generally, which would hide real cleanup failures.
